_readme: Auto-merge rules (ADR 0064, lib/auto_merge_policy.py). This file is itself core: changing it always waits for Gil, so auto-merge can never widen its own permissions. Paths are matched case-insensitively (macOS file systems ignore case). core = always waits for Gil, whatever the ticket; ui = waits until the render check passed (#126); dependencies = manifests and lockfiles: adding or upgrading code from outside always waits. A path under none of these is owned if its top-level folder exists in the repo; a brand-new top-level folder is owned, at most new_top_level_per_week a week. ramp_authors = GitHub logins (any case) whose PRs wait for Gil until that author's own trust ramp opens after 5 clean approvals (ADR 0069 rule 5: mac-mini-2012's bot account; lib/trust_ramp.py). always_ask_authors (optional, still read) = logins whose PRs always wait. A malformed author list makes everything wait.

known_incident_regressions._readme: ADR 0064 amendment (2026-10-26): a rung-3 fix for a regression of a watched incident (lib/auto_merge_regression.py) may merge itself even in core areas, except the paths in still_core (the merge gate and auto-merge itself, so a fix can never loosen the rules that let it merge). It also needs a failing-first regression test, the mutation check, a green main and passing checks, and is re-measured after merge (reverted if the probe still trips). Shadow mode until the owner switches auto-merge on.
